item.title: More Than 100 Years Ago, Black Washingtonians from Anacostia to U Street Influence the Nation Overall
item.description: Black History Month is a reminder of the strength and resilience of African Americans, and their incredible contributions to the nation and world, as highlighted by the Association for the Study of African American Life and History (ASALH) and the Washington Informer. The post More Than 100 Years Ago, Black Washingtonians from Anacostia to U Street Influence the Nation Overall appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: ‘Treemonisha’ Returns: Washington National Opera Reimagines Scott Joplin’s Classic
item.description: Washington National Opera is presenting a newly commissioned adaptation of Scott Joplin's "Treemonisha" at Lisner Auditorium in Washington, D.C., featuring a revised story, musical arrangement and orchestration, and a cast of talented actors. The post ‘Treemonisha’ Returns: Washington National Opera Reimagines Scott Joplin’s Classic appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: 39th AU Summit Emphasizes Need for Water Access, Self-Sufficiency
item.description: The African Union is working to address the lack of access to safe water and sanitation in Africa, through the Africa Water Vision 2063 and Policy framework, the Continental Africa Water Investment Program, and the Africa Water and Sanitation Sector Monitoring Report. The post 39th AU Summit Emphasizes Need for Water Access, Self-Sufficiency appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: After 107 Minutes, Advocates, Politicians Reject Trump’s Narrative
item.description: In his State of the Union address, President Trump touted his accomplishments while Democrats and other critics accused him of misleading the American people with false claims and broken promises. The post After 107 Minutes, Advocates, Politicians Reject Trump’s Narrative appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Crump’s Debut Novel Delivers Big Wins for Black Independent Booksellers
item.description: Attorney Ben Crump's debut novel "Worse Than a Lie" has driven packed signings, sold-out shelves, and a measurable spike in revenue at Black-owned bookstores across the country, with several retailers reporting they exhausted their initial inventory shortly after hosting Crump tour events. The post Crump’s Debut Novel Delivers Big Wins for Black Independent Booksellers appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: With Approval of Federal Disaster Assistance, Potomac Interceptor Restoration on the Horizon
item.description: Local and federal agencies are working together to repair and mitigate the overflow caused by the Potomac Interceptor collapse, with the goal of restoring full functionality and cleaning up the overflow by mid-March. The post With Approval of Federal Disaster Assistance, Potomac Interceptor Restoration on the Horizon appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: The Preservation of Barry Farm: More Than Just the Buildings
item.description: The Barry Farm neighborhood in Northeast D.C. is undergoing a multi-phase redevelopment, with a focus on preserving the area's historic African American legacy and ensuring that the community is at the center of the development process. The post The Preservation of Barry Farm: More Than Just the Buildings appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Family Without Borders: Pew Survey Maps the Depth of Black America’s Kinship Ties
item.description: A new Pew Research Center survey shows that 77% of Black Americans consider someone outside of their biological family to be family, with 95% of those relationships being close friends who have provided support through difficult times. The post Family Without Borders: Pew Survey Maps the Depth of Black America’s Kinship Ties appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Titles, Blood and Breakthroughs at CareFirst Arena
item.description: Davis Boxing Promotions' "The Grind and the Glory" fight card featured nine matches, including a hard-fought win by Erick Rosado over previously undefeated Christopher Glenn, a unanimous decision win by Greg Outlaw over Michael Lee, and a first-round knockout by Keith Saunders Jr. over Lucius Johnson. The post Titles, Blood and Breakthroughs at CareFirst Arena appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: The Great American Departure Gains Speed
item.description: Americans are leaving the U.S. in record numbers, driven by political instability, gun violence, health care costs, and economic anxiety, while immigrants continue to anchor the economy and workforce in cities like Washington, D.C. The post The Great American Departure Gains Speed appeared first on The Washington Informer.
